args.text: [lane-heron] Three risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System) answers for too long: (1) Stale addresses: users are sent to an old server after a site moves, causing outages or errors. (2) Slow recovery: failover to a backup server is delayed because cached answers keep pointing at the failed one. (3) Lingering bad data: a poisoned or hijacked answer stays in the cache and keeps misdirecting users until it expires.

[lane-heron] Idempotent retries matter because networks fail unpredictably, so a client often cannot tell whether a request was processed, and retrying is the only safe way to recover. If the operation is idempotent (repeating it gives the same result as doing it once), a retry cannot cause harm such as double charges or duplicate records.

[lane-heron] Two trade-offs of using UUIDv7 (Universally Unique Identifier, version 7) as a primary key: (1) Larger keys: it takes 16 bytes, against 8 for a typical big integer, so indexes and storage grow and fewer entries fit in memory. (2) Leaked timing: the start of each value encodes its creation time, so anyone who sees an ID can estimate when the record was made, and IDs created in the same millisecond are not strictly ordered unless extra care is taken.

[lane-heron] A write-ahead log is a file where a database records each change before it alters the main data, so nothing is lost if the system crashes part-way through. After a crash, the system replays the log to restore a consistent state.

[lane-heron] Two reasons to pin a client version in a benchmark: (1) Fair comparison: a client update can change speed on its own, so results from different runs would no longer be comparable. (2) Repeatability: others can rerun the same test later and get the same setup, which makes any change in results traceable to what you actually altered.
